title: The planned Motown jazz label and his gospel recording at ABC
summary: Lee says he came to Motown to start a jazz label, and recalls recording gospel for Duke Peacock at ABC.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: But I really came over here to do a jazz label. That was why I left ABC, because my deal here was we're gonna start a jazz label and I was going to do it. That's what I am supposed to start in January.
Yes, uh huh. That's what I was saying -- if you hear about me going to someplace else because they didn't start the jazz label..
Will it be called Motown? Do they have a name?
Well, we're trying to decide what it
will be called. We haven't come up with a name for it yet. But yeah, we're supposed to have it. As a matter of fact, there's a ...
Well, there's a market for it.

Yeah, well, it's all over the street. I've had many, many calls from jazz musicians who want to come with us. But we'll see about that. You know, I did all the gospel over at ABC, also; I did that because I ran in to a lot of young people that I thought had a lot of talent, and no one was recording them, and so I just started recording them for Duke Peacock -- that's the label that ABC acquired.

But all in all, the only reason I changed jobs was because of the carrying of the jazz label. And if you get a chance to build it yourself, then I wont' have to sit around and say what's wrong with the things that Norman Granz Graham does, you know?
